html:
The Tunisian revolution began on 17 December 2010 in the town of Sidi Bouzid, when a street seller, Mohamed Bouazizi, set himself on fire after police took his cart. In four weeks protests drove President Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali from power.

Anger over unemployment, corruption and police abuse spread from the poor interior to Tunis, carried on mobile phones and social media. The army refused to fire on the crowds, and on 14 January 2011 Ben Ali fled to Saudi Arabia after 23 years in power.

The revolution set off the Arab Spring across the region. Tunisia was the only country where it led to a lasting democracy, with a new constitution in 2014 and the National Dialogue. From 2021 President Kais Saied took back much power, rolling back many of its gains.
sum: The Tunisian revolution began on 17 December 2010 in the town of Sidi Bouzid, when a street seller, Mohamed Bouazizi, set himself on fire after police took his cart. In four weeks protests drove President Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali from power.
